01Why now

Why this course, and why now

An agent is a system component that makes decisions at run time, which changes how you design, test and secure everything around it. This level treats agents as architecture, not as a feature: what they may do, what they must never do, how you know they work, and how you stop them.

02Outcomes

What you will be able to do

Choose the right shape

Decide when a fixed workflow is better than an agent, and how much autonomy to grant.

Design the boundaries

Define tools, permissions, memory and budgets for an agent system.

Prove it works

Plan evaluations and tracing so you can measure an agent, not just watch it.

Document for agents

Write architecture notes that people and coding agents can both read.

04The lab

Your agent system design

Design and document an agent system for a real task in your own field, with limits you can defend. One project, built in steps after each lesson. Each step has instructions, a finished example, a health check, and saves on your device.

The steps

  1. Describe the task and decide workflow or agent
  2. Define the tools and their contracts
  3. Set permissions, budgets and approval points
  4. Design the memory and context
  5. Write the evaluation plan
  6. Write the architecture note an agent could read

What the health check looks for

  • Every tool has a contract and a permission
  • There is a stated limit on cost and on actions
  • The evaluation plan names a measurable pass mark
